tasks.task: check disk on 5 hosts (discover + fan out)
tasks.note: run_on_many already saves 5 calls; response metadata still costs ~959 tok. Compact list + compact fan-out would cost 296 tok. Calling run_command per host would cost 181 tok/host (905 tok, 5 calls).

tasks.task: tail a log (agent asks for last 50 lines)
tasks.note: Works today with "| tail -n 50". Without tail in the command, the default cap returns 22,710 tok (67,549 chars, truncated at 64 KiB). 50 lines already costs 5,476 tok; 20 lines costs 2,296 tok.

tasks.task: edit one line in a 20 KiB config
tasks.note: No read/edit tool: the agent cats 5,537 tok, emits the whole file (5,537 tok output), rewrites it, then verifies. A read_remote_file(offset,limit) + replace_in_remote_file would need ~40 lines + ~20 tok ack + verify.
One compound command works without sudo. With sudo the failure (240 tok) is classified as "unknown" and the hint does not mention tty:true; retrying with tty burns a timeout.

tasks.task: find which of 10 hosts has an error
tasks.note: Answer is one alias, but every host carries ~19 fields. Compact = 153 tok; a matched-only reply ({matched:[{alias:"web04",count:7}]}) is ~20 tok. 50 hosts costs 8,894 tok (28,709 chars) for an answer that is a list of failing aliases.
sed works (4,525 tok). No read_remote_file means the agent must know sed/awk and shell-quote; a read_remote_file(offset,limit) would be discoverable and would not mangle binary data.

tasks.task: recover from a typo in an alias
tasks.note: "Alias not found" returns no hint, no candidates and no errorKind; the agent must list the store (2,710 tok for 10 connections; compact list 213 tok) or guess again. Three closest aliases in the error would cost ~20 tok.

tasks.task: fleet check (50 hosts, one line each)
tasks.note: 8,294 tok for 50 one-word answers; compact results = 713 tok; a failures-only summary = 16 tok.
